content_voiceover: This slide covers maintenance therapy and second line treatment for mantle cell lymphoma. After high dose therapy with autologous stem cell rescue, or after aggressive induction, maintenance consists of rituximab every eight weeks for three years, with the option to add a covalent BTK inhibitor, acalabrutinib, ibrutinib, or zanubrutinib, for a fixed two year duration, reflecting data showing improved outcomes when BTKi is layered onto post transplant maintenance. After less aggressive induction, maintenance is simpler, rituximab every eight weeks for two to three years following CHOP rituximab or bendamustine rituximab, though maintenance hasn't been formally evaluated after VR-CAP. For second line and subsequent therapy, preferred options are covalent BTK inhibitors, acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib continuously, or lenalidomide plus rituximab, with ibrutinib plus or minus rituximab as another recommended option. When disease progresses after a prior covalent BTKi, the pathway shifts to non-covalent BTK inhibition with pirtobrutinib, or to T cell mediated therapies including CD19 directed CAR T cell products, brexucabtagene autoleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel, and bispecific antibodies like glofitamab or mosunetuzumab combined with polatuzumab vedotin. Other second line options useful in certain circumstances include bendamustine rituximab if not previously used, bortezomib, DHAP style platinum regimens, GEMOX, and venetoclax with or without rituximab.
keypoints: Post-transplant or post-aggressive induction: rituximab plus fixed-duration covalent BTKi maintenance
Post-less-aggressive induction: rituximab maintenance for two to three years
Second line preferred: covalent BTK inhibitors or lenalidomide plus rituximab
Progression after covalent BTKi: switch to non-covalent BTKi pirtobrutinib
Later options include CD19 CAR T cell therapy and bispecific antibodies
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the sequencing logic: covalent BTKi maintenance follows aggressive induction or transplant, covalent BTKi remains preferred in second line, and once a patient progresses on a covalent BTKi, you move to pirtobrutinib, CAR T cell therapy, or bispecific antibodies.
